merger_description:
Saint-Gobain S.A. (Saint-Gobain), through its indirect wholly-owned Canadian subsidiary CertainTeed Canada, Inc. (CertainTeed), proposes to acquire 100% of the shares of Xypex Investment Holdings Inc. (the **Acquisition**).

CertainTeed is a Canada-headquartered manufacturer of building products and an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Saint-Gobain. In Australia, Saint-Gobain supplies a range of interior and exterior building products through its subsidiary CSR Building Products Pty Ltd and other companies. Saint-Gobain’s subsidiary GCP Australia Pty Ltd (GCP) provides specialty construction chemicals and building materials in Australia across two segments: (a) chemical admixtures, supplied through its "Chryso" division; and (b) construction repair and renovation products, including waterproofing membranes, mortars, and other building technologies. GCP supplies its products nationally and operates three manufacturing plants in New South Wales, Queensland and Victoria.

Xypex Chemical Corporation (Xypex) is a Canadian manufacturer specialising in concrete waterproofing protection and repair technologies. Xypex operates in Australia through XCC Holdings Pty Ltd and its subsidiaries, Concrete Waterproofing Manufacturing Pty Ltd and National Concrete Solutions Pty Ltd. Xypex supplies (a) waterproofing chemical crystalline admixtures and (b) surface-applied fine mortars and mortar products used for concrete repair, and restoration mortars, using the same crystalline technology. Xypex supplies its products nationally from its manufacturing site in Albury, New South Wales, and maintains warehouses in Brisbane, Sydney, Melbourne and Perth. National Concrete Solutions is a specialist concrete remediation contractor that applies Xypex's products on construction projects and supplies concrete asset management services.

determination_table_content.details:
Chemical admixtures are products that are added to concrete during
mixing to enhance or modify specific properties of the concrete such
as workability, strength and durability.
When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form and publicly available information.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition would be unlikely to have
the effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings:
• The parties do not appear to be close competitors in the supply
of chemical admixtures or mortar products as their products
have different functionalities.
• The merged entity would continue to face competition from
several alternative suppliers of chemical admixtures and mortar
products in Australia.
